A1_2.evidence: v2.1 open case: the deposit is fully open (pack 'access_right': 'open') and requires no authentication; no access control exists or is warranted for analysis scripts, so the sole 0 case (control warranted but undocumented/unjustified) does not arise.

A2.evidence: Code sits in a Zenodo record covered by Row 2 persistence entitlements - tombstone page on withdrawal with DOI and URL retained, files preserved on retraction, metadata always publicly accessible - rather than on a bare GitHub/GitLab URL, which Row 5 gives no persistence entitlement of any kind.

(v.4.2.2)', quanteda), and analytical parameters and formulae (skip distance 'k value for all generated skipgrams is thus set to 13'; the expected-frequency and PMI equations), plus the deposit's structured metadata record. R1_1.evidence: Licence identified for the deposit that carries the code: pack reports licences ['cc-by-4.0'] at both Zenodo and DataCite with licence_conflicts empty; the paper is silent on a separate code licence, so per the v2.1 rule the artefact is scored on the licence recorded at the hosting service. (CC-BY-4.0 is an unusual choice for software but is clear, accessible and machine-identifiable, which is what R1.1 requires.)

R1_2.evidence: Provenance of the computational workflow is documented: creators and date via the deposit record (publication_year 2024), a version lineage (two versions under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10623549, records 10623550 and 10801706), the exact runtime and package used, the parameter settings (k = 13; 2-, 3-, 4-gram levels), the stated absence of significance thresholding ('rather than working with arbitrary thresholds of significance'), and the code deposited together with the inputs it consumes and the tables it produces.

R1_3.evidence: None of the instrument's code-specific qualifying standards is evidenced: no package structure, no CITATION.cff, no CodeMeta, and no community review of the authors' own scripts (the deposit is a Zenodo record typed 'dataset', not a CRAN/JOSS/rOpenSci-reviewed package). quanteda's JOSS review attaches to a third-party dependency, which the aggregation rule bars from substituting for the paper's own analysis scripts. Looked for these markers in the paper's statements and in the pack's harvested fields; none present.

F2.evidence: Structured repository metadata record verified at two granting services: pack fields 'metadata_record': true with publisher 'Zenodo', publication_year 2024, resource_type 'Dataset', rights (cc-by-4.0), access_right 'open', state 'findable'. F3.evidence: Pack records both report 'identifier_in_metadata': true for 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 and 10.5281/zenodo.10801706 - the DOI is carried inside the metadata record that describes the deposit (rung (i), corroborated by Row 1 entitlement that a DataCite metadata record carrying the identifier exists).

F4.evidence: Indexed in searchable registries named by the instrument (Zenodo, DataCite): pack shows successful resolution at both api.datacite.org (http_status 200, state 'findable') and zenodo.org/api/records/10623550 (http_status 200).

I1.evidence: The deposit pairs executable analysis scripts with the tables they consume: 'Dedicated R code and complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3' and 'All code and data are available here'. The data are, by the paper's own description, a formal tabular/textual representation - binary presence/absence coding of motif types transcribed per artefact, transformed into whitespace-delimited motif strings ('A1 B10 C1 E1 F5 F7 F10 F12 F14 F49') read by R/quanteda - i.e. machine-parseable, not narrative or image data. Inference basis is stated explicitly: file-level formats were not directly inspected, but code that runs on the deposited tables entails a structured representation.

I2.evidence: No FAIR vocabulary is used. Motif terms come from 'Płonka's (2003, pp. 315-325) own motif classification scheme ... (named A1, A2, etc.)' - an idiosyncratic scheme published in a printed monograph with no PIDs, no machine-readable serialisation, and no registry. Chronological units (Maglemose, Kongemose, Ertebølle) and place names are free text; no PeriodO, Getty AAT, ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM or comparable PID-bearing vocabulary is cited anywhere in Methods or the availability statements. Looked for vocabulary citations, URIs and conformance statements; none found.

I3.evidence: No qualified, PID-bearing reference from the data to other resources is evidenced. The dataset's stated per-object linkage is to 'original source' in the analogue catalogue (Table 3 column 'Figure in Płonka (2003)'), and the Płonka (2003) reference carries no DOI or other PID, so the derivation relation is not PID-qualified. The pack reports no relatedIdentifier fields, and Zenodo Row 2 grants no related-identifier entitlement; the reported concept_doi 10.5281/zenodo.10623549 is an auto-generated intra-record version lineage, not a qualified reference to another resource.

R1.evidence: Plurality of relevant attributes documented at rung (i): 'These data consist of numerous categorical variables corresponding to the characteristics of each ornamented object and associated metadata such as location, quality of contextual information, and original source', and 'We do include pertinent metadata such as artefact classes, chronology, and spatial distribution'. Section 2.1 sets out the classification scheme, coding rule and corpus construction; the Zenodo record adds a structured creator/title/date/type/rights metadata layer.

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified, not merely present as a field: pack reports licences ['cc-by-4.0'] at both DataCite and Zenodo for 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 and 10.5281/zenodo.10801706, with licence_conflicts empty. Per the v2.1 per-artefact rule, the deposit is scored on its own recorded licence (the article's CC BY and Elsevier TDM licences govern the article, a clean division rather than a conflict). Zenodo's default-licence footnote is interpretive only - a default-valued CC-BY-4.0 is fully operative.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance: source named and cited ('the comprehensive catalogue of Mesolithic ornamentation compiled by Płonka (2003)'), creation process stated ('the South Scandinavian data were manually extracted and digitised'), transformation chain documented (presence/absence coding transcribed from pp. 315-325, then 'transformed from presence/absence coding into a sentence-imitating structure'), processing environment and versions pinned ('R programming environment (v.4.2.2)', 'Quanteda package'), and parameters given ('the k value for all generated skipgrams is thus set to 13') - with the generating code deposited alongside the data.

R1_3.evidence: R1.3 route (a), 'generic metadata schemas (DataCite, Dublin Core)', is satisfied at deposit level: the pack verifies a resolving DataCite metadata record for the deposit (http_status 200, state 'findable', identifier_in_metadata true), and Zenodo Row 2 entitles DataCite metadata by construction. Scored as deposit-level standard conformance only; the paper's methodological standards (PMI, skipgram practice) are expressly excluded by the R1.3 boundary, and no domain schema (ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM) or accredited-domain-repository route (Row 4) applies here.
